disease_context: TP53 is mutated in over 50% of all human cancers, acting as the 'guardian of the genome'. Loss of p53 function allows cells to bypass apoptosis and accumulate oncogenic mutations.
difficulty_rationale: Intrinsically disordered N- and C-termini, large flat protein-protein interaction surface, no deep binding pockets; most small-molecule approaches target the DNA-binding domain mutant restoration.

known_drugs.name: APR-246 (Eprenetapopt)
known_drugs.mechanism: Converts mutant p53 to wild-type-like conformation, restoring apoptosis

known_drugs.name: AMG 232
known_drugs.mechanism: MDM2 inhibitor releasing p53 from negative regulation

known_drugs.name: Nutlin-3a
known_drugs.mechanism: MDM2 antagonist, stabilises p53

disease_context: BRCA1 is a tumour suppressor involved in DNA double-strand break repair via homologous recombination. Germline mutations dramatically increase lifetime risk of breast and ovarian cancer.
difficulty_rationale: Large multi-domain scaffold protein; therapeutic strategy focuses on synthetic lethality (PARP inhibitors) rather than direct BRCA1 targeting. Very few druggable pockets on the protein itself.

known_drugs.name: Olaparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP inhibitor exploiting BRCA1 deficiency via synthetic lethality

known_drugs.name: Niraparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor, approved for BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer

known_drugs.name: Talazoparib
known_drugs.mechanism: PARP inhibitor with PARP trapping activity

disease_context: EGFR is overexpressed or mutated in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), colorectal, and head/neck cancers. Activating mutations in exons 19-21 drive kinase-dependent proliferation.
difficulty_rationale: Well-validated kinase target with a defined ATP-binding pocket. Resistance mutations (T790M, C797S) complicate drug design but multiple generations of inhibitors have been developed.

known_drugs.name: Erlotinib
known_drugs.mechanism: First-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), reversible ATP-competitive

known_drugs.name: Afatinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Second-generation irreversible EGFR/HER2 TKI

known_drugs.name: Osimertinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Third-generation TKI targeting T790M resistance mutation, covalent C797

known_drugs.name: Cetuximab
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody blocking ligand binding

disease_context: HER2 (ERBB2) is amplified in ~20% of breast cancers and gastric cancers, driving aggressive tumour growth. HER2-positive breast cancer has poor prognosis without targeted therapy.
difficulty_rationale: Well-characterised kinase domain; multiple approved drugs. Main challenge is identifying molecules that overcome lapatinib/trastuzumab resistance and CNS penetration.

known_drugs.name: Trastuzumab (Herceptin)
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody, blocks extracellular domain IV

known_drugs.name: Lapatinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Dual EGFR/HER2 TKI, reversible ATP-competitive

known_drugs.name: Pertuzumab
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-HER2 antibody blocking domain II dimerisation

known_drugs.name: Neratinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Irreversible pan-HER TKI

disease_context: KRAS is the most frequently mutated oncogene in human cancer (~25% overall), particularly pancreatic (90%), colorectal (40%), and lung cancers (30%). G12C, G12D, and G12V mutations lock KRAS in the active GTP-bound state.
difficulty_rationale: Historically considered 'undruggable' due to picomolar GTP affinity and featureless surface. The G12C covalent pocket discovery was a breakthrough, but G12D/G12V remain extremely difficult.

known_drugs.name: Sotorasib (AMG510)
known_drugs.mechanism: First covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor, locks in GDP-bound inactive state

known_drugs.name: Adagrasib (MRTX849)
known_drugs.mechanism: Covalent irreversible KRAS G12C inhibitor

known_drugs.name: MRTX1133
known_drugs.mechanism: Non-covalent KRAS G12D inhibitor (clinical trials)

disease_context: BCL2 is an anti-apoptotic protein overexpressed in follicular lymphoma (t(14;18) translocation), CLL, and many solid tumours. It sequesters pro-apoptotic proteins BIM, BAX, and BAK to block programmed cell death.
difficulty_rationale: BH3-binding hydrophobic groove is a validated drug target. Venetoclax demonstrates proof-of-concept; main challenge is selectivity among BCL2 family members (BCL-XL, MCL1).

known_drugs.name: Venetoclax (ABT-199)
known_drugs.mechanism: BH3 mimetic selectively targeting BCL2, displaces pro-apoptotic BIM

known_drugs.name: Navitoclax (ABT-263)
known_drugs.mechanism: BCL2/BCL-XL dual inhibitor

known_drugs.name: Oblimersen
known_drugs.mechanism: BCL2 antisense oligonucleotide

disease_context: CDK4 partners with cyclin D1 to phosphorylate RB1 and drive G1→S cell cycle progression. Amplified in ~15% of cancers (liposarcoma, breast, lung); constitutively active CDK4/6 enables uncontrolled proliferation.
difficulty_rationale: Deep, well-defined ATP-binding pocket with good selectivity features. Multiple approved drugs demonstrate high tractability. Main challenge is selectivity over CDK6.

known_drugs.name: Palbociclib (Ibrance)
known_drugs.mechanism: Selective CDK4/6 inhibitor, arrests cell cycle at G1

known_drugs.name: Ribociclib (Kisqali)
known_drugs.mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibitor for HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer

known_drugs.name: Abemaciclib (Verzenio)
known_drugs.mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibitor with greater CDK4 selectivity

disease_context: VEGFR2 (KDR) is the primary mediator of VEGF-driven tumour angiogenesis. Solid tumours upregulate VEGF to recruit new blood vessels; blocking VEGFR2 starves the tumour of nutrients and oxygen.
difficulty_rationale: Well-validated kinase target with approved multi-kinase inhibitors. Selectivity over other VEGFR family members and off-target kinases (PDGFR, c-Kit) is the key design challenge.

known_drugs.name: Sunitinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Multi-targeted VEGFR/PDGFR/c-Kit TKI

known_drugs.name: Sorafenib
known_drugs.mechanism: RAF/VEGFR2/PDGFR TKI blocking angiogenesis and proliferation

known_drugs.name: Pazopanib
known_drugs.mechanism: VEGFR1/2/3, PDGFR, c-Kit inhibitor

known_drugs.name: Axitinib
known_drugs.mechanism: Potent selective VEGFR1/2/3 inhibitor

disease_context: PD-L1 is expressed on tumour cells and tumour-associated macrophages to suppress anti-tumour T-cell immunity via PD-1 engagement. Checkpoint inhibition targeting PD-L1 has revolutionised treatment of melanoma, NSCLC, and many other cancers.
difficulty_rationale: IgV-like domain has a well-characterised CC' loop binding interface for PD-1. Small-molecule disruptors of the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction have been developed and entered clinical trials, validating druggability.

known_drugs.name: Atezolizumab (Tecentriq)
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody blocking PD-1/PD-L1 interaction

known_drugs.name: Durvalumab (Imfinzi)
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 antibody, also blocks CD80 interaction

known_drugs.name: Avelumab (Bavencio)
known_drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 IgG1 antibody with ADCC activity

disease_context: MDM2 is the principal negative regulator of p53, targeting it for proteasomal degradation. MDM2 is amplified in ~7% of all cancers (especially liposarcoma and osteosarcoma), enabling tumour cells to silence p53.
difficulty_rationale: The p53-binding hydrophobic cleft on MDM2 is one of the best characterised protein-protein interaction drug targets. Multiple clinical-stage inhibitors with sub-nanomolar affinity have been developed.

known_drugs.name: Idasanutlin (RG7388)
known_drugs.mechanism: Potent selective MDM2 antagonist, displaces p53 Phe19/Trp23/Leu26 triad

known_drugs.name: Milademetan (DS-3032b)
known_drugs.mechanism: MDM2 inhibitor with broad solid tumour activity

known_drugs.name: Navtemadlin (AMG-232)
known_drugs.mechanism: Picomolar MDM2/MDMX dual inhibitor
